newsitem.title: FRANCE: MOTOR RACING-JOEST STABLE LOOK FOR ANOTHER 24 HOURS VICTORY.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-JOEST STABLE LOOK FOR ANOTHER 24 HOURS VICTORY.

text.p: The Joest stable will be looking for a repeat victory in the Le Mans 24-hour race this weekend with ex-Formula One driver Michele Alboreto taking pole in a Porsche-powered car.

Alboreto, in an open sports prototype built by Britain's Tom Walkinshaw similar to the car which won last year with German Manuel Reuter, American Davey Jones and Austrian Alexander Wurz at the wheel, smashed the qualifying record for the 13.6-km circuit by five seconds on Thursday.

"Pole position does not mean much for a race like this but the car looks fine and I'm confident," said the Italian veteran, who will share the drive with Swedes Stefan Johanson and Tom Kristensen. "I think we should be regarded as favourites."
Joest are aiming for a fourth victory, having achieved their first wins in 1984 and 1985, while Porsche can extend to 15 their record number of victories in the sports-car classic.
The 65th Le Mans 24-hours starts at 1400 GMT on Saturday with 48 entries.
Although a prototype has taken pole position, factory GTs, mainstay of the event since the demise of the world endurance championship, take up the next six places on the grid.

Belgian veteran Thierry Boutsen and experienced partners Hans Stuck of Germany and Bob Wollek of France start in second place after a marginal improvement in their qualifying time in Thursday's final session in their Porsche GT.
They clocked 3:43.363, less than two seconds behind Alboreto, while the Nissan R390 driven in qualifying by another Belgian, Eric van de Poele, starts third.
The prototypes have a very thin international calendar these days, which does not allow them the technical advances they once enjoyed.
A prototype driver, Frenchman Sebastien Enjolras, was killed in a spectacular crash during pre-qualifying tests early last month.
"It will be more difficult for prototypes this year but if we didn't think we could win we wouldn't be here," Alboreto said.
The French stable of Yves Courage, often in victory contention at Le Mans but always unlucky, pin their hopes on American father and son Mario and Michael Andretti and Frenchman Olivier Grouillard.
"It's the one race my father hasn't won," Michael Andretti said. "Winning Le Mans has been his dream for years and we'll do our best to make it come true."
